What is Lokalise AI?

Developer-first localisation management platform with an AI layer that translates strings with awareness of product context, screenshots, glossary and tone of voice - built for software teams shipping continuously rather than for document translation.

Best for

Continuous software string localisation inside a CI/CD pipeline.

Main features

  • AI translation with context awareness (screenshots, key comments, previous translations)
  • Lokalise AI quality scoring and automatic post-editing
  • translation memory and glossary
  • in-context editor showing strings in the live UI
  • branching and CI/CD integration
  • screenshot-based context capture
  • QA checks for placeholders, length and terminology
  • role-based workflows and approvals.

Practical use cases

  • Localising app strings on every release without blocking the pipeline
  • keeping UI copy consistent across 15 languages
  • catching placeholder and truncation bugs before release
  • managing translator review workflow inside a sprint.

Who is it for?

  • Software engineering and product teams, localisation managers at SaaS companies, mobile app teams.

Pricing, free access & limits

Per-seat subscription with key/word volume tiers; AI translation metered separately

Plans described in the source

Start tier around $140/mo, Essential around $270-450/mo, Pro around $990/mo, Enterprise custom - all varying by seat count and hosted key volume, billed annually for the best rate. Lokalise AI translation is typically metered as an add-on by word or credit volume. Free trial available. Verify current tiers - Lokalise repositions its plans regularly.

Free plan

No permanent free plan for teams; a free trial and limited free options for open-source projects.

Free trial

Yes - 14-day free trial, no card required for most tiers.

Usage limits to consider

Plans are bounded by seats and hosted keys; AI translation words are metered separately from the seat fee. Higher tiers unlock advanced QA, branching and SSO.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Context awareness genuinely improves AI output over generic MT - screenshots and key comments make a measurable difference
  • best-in-class developer workflow with real CI/CD integration
  • the in-context editor eliminates a whole class of layout bugs
  • strong QA checks.

Limitations to consider

  • Expensive - entry pricing is well above Smartcat or Crowdin for small teams
  • priced for software strings, not documents
  • steep setup investment before value appears
  • AI word metering on top of seat cost makes total cost hard to predict
  • no meaningful free tier.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web
  • CLI
  • SDKs
  • API

Languages

  • Unlimited target languages; Arabic RTL and French fully supported with RTL layout handling

API access

Yes - comprehensive REST API, CLI, OTA SDKs for iOS/Android, and GitHub/GitLab Actions

Integrations and exports

  • GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Figma, Sketch, Adobe XD, Contentful, WordPress, Intercom, Zendesk, Jira, Slack, Amplitude

Evaluation notes

The screenshot-context feature is what separates Lokalise AI from generic MT - if you will not invest in capturing context, most of the premium is wasted. Best-fit is a product team already doing continuous delivery.
